headline: Marriage not independently established
assessment: The original archive retains an older account describing a completed marriage. The strongest currently identified dated record is a *marriage intention* for James Beveridge and Jean White of Georgetown, not a marriage certificate. The original ceremony and a unique identity link to the 1724 Marblehead-born James have not been established.

sources.title: Brunswick marriage intentions 1740–1764, printed town transcription
sources.supports: Printed 1749 intention naming James Beveridge and Jean White of Georgetown; not a marriage certificate.

original_record_needed: Locate the dated Georgetown/Brunswick solemnization or church marriage register and establish both parties' independent identities.
display_title: James Beveridge and Jean White announce their intention to marry (ceremony unverified)
display_summary: A surviving printed transcription records a marriage intention for James Beveridge and Jean White of Georgetown on February 6, 1749. This is not proof that a wedding occurred or that the named James is the Marblehead-born James Beveridge (1724).
display_evidence_status: Documented marriage intention; ceremony and identities not established

headline: Town vital-record transcription corroborates the date
assessment: A published transcription of Marblehead town vital records includes Sarah Bennett and James Beveridge (variant recorded as 'Beseridge') married 16 December 1723. This supports a historical marriage entry but not the asserted Scottish birthplace of James Sr. or a complete ancestral migration chain.

sources.title: Vital Records of Marblehead to 1849, marriage list (published town records)
sources.supports: Town marriage list under Bennett Sarah, 16 Dec 1723, surname spelling variants.

original_record_needed: Compare the original Marblehead civil/church register folio; do not infer James's Scottish parents from the surname or date.
display_title: Recorded marriage of James Beveridge and Sarah Bennett, Marblehead
display_summary: The published transcription of Marblehead town vital records records James Beveridge and Sarah Bennett marrying on December 16, 1723. The specific church location and James's place of birth are not independently established by this marriage entry.
display_evidence_status: Published transcription of a town marriage entry

headline: Marblehead town birth entry corroborates James's date
assessment: Marblehead's published vital records list James, son of James and Sarah (spelled Befreadge/Befridge), born 27 August 1724. This supports a parent-child entry in the Massachusetts household but does not identify him uniquely with the James in the 1749 Georgetown marriage-intention list.

sources.title: Marblehead Vital Records, births, published transcription
sources.supports: Birth of James to James and Sarah, 27 Aug 1724, town record published under variant spelling.

original_record_needed: Verify original town register entry and any later migration deed/probate tying the 1724 child to the 1749 Maine James.
display_title: Birth of James, son of James and Sarah, in Marblehead (later identity uncertain)
display_summary: The published Marblehead town birth transcription names James, son of James and Sarah (Befreadge/Befridge variants), born August 27, 1724. Further evidence is needed to identify this child as the James Beveridge named in the 1749 Georgetown marriage intention.
display_evidence_status: Published transcription of a town birth entry; later identity uncertain

headline: Mercy's maiden surname and approximate age attested, but parents not verified
assessment: An inherited archive event claimed Mercy Beveridge Henry was the daughter of James Beveridge Jr. and Jean McKinney White and spouse of 'Henry Henry'. Later inspection of the 1930 Topsham cemetery transcription establishes a Mercy [Beveridge], wife of James, who died in 1831 aged 78 years 6 months. It supports approximate 1753 birth year, not a January 1 birthdate, Topsham birthplace, original parentage, or a Vinalhaven death. The site displays source-corrected data; it retains the imported claim in the unaltered original archive for provenance.

sources.title: Maine Historical Society Topsham vital records, vol. II, Henry death list (1930)
sources.supports: Gravestone-derived death 26 Oct 1831 aged 78 years 6 months; indexed married surname Henry and maiden name Beveridge.

sources.title: Maine official cemetery survey, First Parish Cemetery (entry 139.1)
sources.supports: Documents reported Mercy Beveridge Henry burial and spouse James; derivative of same grave, not a second independent original certificate.

original_record_needed: Locate actual Mercy birth/baptism register or parent-naming probate and photograph original gravestone; do not assign her to James/Jean's children without direct evidence.
display_title: Approximate birth period of Mercy (Beveridge) Henry — parents unknown
display_summary: Mercy Beveridge Henry died in 1831 aged about 78 years and six months according to a gravestone transcription, suggesting a birth around 1753. Her birth parents and birthplace have not been proved. Later sources identify James Henry as her husband.
display_evidence_status: Birth year inferred from gravestone age; parentage unverified
